ca_m_the_weeping_wall.blurb: A tall, smooth slab on Suicide Rock above Idyllwild, rising roughly 300 feet with climbs of up to three pitches. All 15 routes here are traditional lines, and the grades stay moderate: a single easy outlier and one 5.8, then mostly 5.9 and 5.10. The face is slabby rather than steep, so expect delicate friction and sparse protection instead of power. The trail from the road leads to the base of the rock, and the wall is visible through the trees once you arrive. It suits climbers comfortable on slabs who want longer routes without leaving the moderate range.

ca_mad_max_boulder.blurb: The standout boulder of the Mad Max Area, in the Hartley Springs country above June Lake at around 8,200 feet. It holds 15 problems on a steep south face, ranging from a couple of very easy ones up through V7 and into V9, with three problems at V7. Trees shade the face, so it stays pleasant on warm summer days. The lines are tall enough that pads and spotters matter. The other boulders nearby are shorter and gentler, so they make a useful warm-up before you step onto this one.

ca_lost_wall.blurb: A steep wall on Mariuolumne Dome in Tuolumne Meadows, at about 9,800 feet, just right of the Nazgul Wall. The 15 routes are all traditional, running from 5.6 up to a single 5.11, with the largest cluster at 5.10 and a fair spread of 5.7 to 5.9 below that. A broad roof covers many lines on the left side, while a headwall sits to the right. A few routes are multi-pitch. Protection is decent by Tuolumne standards, though some lines are bold, and first bolts can sit high. The base is a wide flat platform, which makes it comfortable for a group.

ca_left_wall_2.blurb: The sunnier, drier side of The Wedge, the main wall on El Cajon Mountain in San Diego County. It has 15 routes, nine sport and six trad, graded from 5.6 to 5.10 with most of them at 5.10. Several are multi-pitch, including four- and five-pitch lines. It gets sun for most of the day, so summer outings run hot and need plenty of water. The walk in is long, an hour to an hour and a half with about 1,800 feet of gain. Loose rock knocked by other parties is a real concern, so a helmet is wise.

ca_north_buttress_2.blurb: The longer eastern ridge of two that run north from Cathedral Peak above Tuolumne Meadows, at roughly 9,200 feet. Its toe sits close to the busy trail to Cathedral Lakes, a walk of around 40 to 50 minutes from the road. Of the 15 routes, nearly all are alpine-style trad with one sport line, graded 5.5 to 5.10, and most fall between 5.7 and 5.9. Older lines show their age, but it saw little traffic until new routes went in around 2014; the newer climbs are on the west and north sides near the base. Expect a quieter alternative to the famous southeast buttress.

ca_windy_wall.blurb: A quieter wall in the Buttermilk Crags outside Bishop, reached by a short hike northeast from the backside parking, roughly 15 minutes. It faces west and sits tucked behind the busier faces. The 15 routes mix cracks and bolted faces, ten trad and five sport, with grades from 5.5 to 5.10. Seven of them are 5.10, and the rest are spread across the easier grades, so beginners and mid-grade climbers both find something. Expect an exposed, dry high-desert setting where afternoon winds often pick up. It is a good pick for a calm day away from the Buttermilks crowds.

ca_sunshine_face_left_side.blurb: The far-left part of the Sunshine Face on Suicide Rock above Idyllwild, set past and above the big break of Paisano Chimney and half hidden around the corner from the main face. Reach it by walking along the base of the wall. The golden face here holds some of the hardest face climbing on the rock. Of 15 routes, 12 are trad, plus one each of aid, sport and top rope. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, but the bulk sit at 5.11 and 5.12, so it leans toward strong climbers, with a few easier chimneys and cracks.
